skill.name: backend-api
skill.description: Design RESTful API endpoints with clear routes, HTTP methods, status codes, query parameters, middleware, versioning, and documentation guidance.
skill.summary: Guide REST API endpoint design, routing, versioning, status codes, middleware, and documentation.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: One static finding was confirmed. SKILL.md instructs the agent to follow a relative link outside the skill directory, which creates an unsafe filesystem dependency. No evidence of prompt injection, network activity, command execution, or data exfiltration was found.

remediation.suggestion: Move api.md into the skill package or replace the upward relative path with packaged instructions.

finding_verdicts.reason: The instruction tells the agent to read ../../../agent-os/standards/backend/api.md, an upward relative path outside the skill package. That can cause filesystem access outside the packaged skill and makes the skill depend on untrusted parent paths.

high_findings.title: Path traversal sequence
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction tells the agent to read ../../../agent-os/standards/backend/api.md, an upward relative path outside the skill package. That can cause filesystem access outside the packaged skill and makes the skill depend on untrusted parent paths.

content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent routes, status codes, and request patterns. This skill guides REST API design, endpoint changes, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation and modification of backend API routes and controllers.
Applies RESTful resource naming, URL structure, and API versioning practices.
Supports HTTP method selection, status code handling, and response formatting.
Covers query parameters for filtering, sorting, and pagination.
Addresses API middleware for authentication, validation, rate limiting, and usage tracking.
Helps prepare API documentation and OpenAPI or Swagger specifications.
limitations: The packaged skill references a standards document outside its folder.
It provides guidance, not runnable server code or generated tests.
It is focused on REST and HTTP APIs, not GraphQL or event streams.
It cannot verify production behavior without access to the target application.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Resource Endpoint
use_cases.description: Define routes, methods, request fields, response behavior, and status codes for a new backend resource.

use_cases.title: Standardize Existing Routes
use_cases.description: Review route names, nesting, versioning, and query parameters for consistency across a service.

use_cases.title: Prepare API Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn endpoint behavior into clear documentation for client teams and OpenAPI specifications.

prompt_templates.title: Create Endpoint Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design REST endpoints for a new resource named [resource]. Include routes, methods, status codes, and response behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new API resource

prompt_templates.title: Review Route Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these API routes for REST consistency. Check naming, nesting, methods, query parameters, and versioning.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing backend service

prompt_templates.title: Design Middleware Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose middleware for authentication, validation, rate limiting, and usage tracking for this API surface.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for shared API concerns

prompt_templates.title: Modernize API Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this API contract for consistent resources, pagination, error responses, status codes, and documentation updates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced API cleanup across multiple endpoints

output_examples.input: Design endpoints for customer orders with pagination and status filters.
output: A resource plan with collection and item routes.
Recommended methods for listing, creating, updating, and deleting orders.
Pagination and filtering guidance for order status and date ranges.
Status code guidance for successful, invalid, unauthorized, and missing resources.

output_examples.input: Review route naming for a versioned inventory API.
output: A consistency review of route names and resource boundaries.
Suggestions for version placement and nested resource depth.
Notes about query parameters for sorting and filtering.
Documentation updates needed for client teams.

best_practices: Use resource nouns for URLs and reserve verbs for HTTP methods.
Define status codes, error shapes, and pagination behavior before implementation.
Document authentication, validation, rate limits, and response examples with each endpoint.
anti_patterns: Do not mix action names into URLs when a resource model fits.
Do not add nested routes that hide ownership or make authorization unclear.
Do not ship endpoint changes without updating API documentation.

faq.question: What type of APIs does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports RESTful HTTP APIs, including routes, methods, status codes, query parameters, middleware, and documentation.

faq.question: Can it generate production server code?
faq.answer: It guides design and implementation decisions, but it does not provide a runnable framework template by itself.

faq.question: Does it support API documentation work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help describe endpoint behavior and prepare OpenAPI or Swagger specifications.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review route structure, versioning, query parameters, middleware, and consistency.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication and rate limiting?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for API middleware, authentication checks, validation, rate limiting, and usage tracking.

faq.question: What should users check before publishing this skill?
faq.answer: Users should package the referenced backend API standards inside the skill or remove the upward relative path.
